hook.text: In the 1800s, milk killed thousands of children every year. Tuberculosis, typhoid, and diphtheria lurked inside.

buildup.text: Raw milk from urban dairies was a breeding ground for bacteria. Cows lived in filthy conditions.

discovery.text: Louis Pasteur showed that heating milk to 72°C for 15 seconds killed dangerous pathogens without ruining taste.

twist.text: Dairy companies fought pasteurization for decades—it cost money and they preferred blaming consumers.

climax.text: Mandatory pasteurization became law in most countries by mid-1900s. Child milk-borne deaths plummeted.

punchline.text: Heating milk for 15 seconds saved millions of lives.

quiz.question: What does pasteurization do to milk?
options: Heats it briefly to kill dangerous pathogens
